title: Swedish Meatball Cream Gravy
description: A toasted butter roux and warm pinches of allspice and nutmeg give this Swedish-style brown gravy its familiar meatball-shop flavor.

ingredients.name: low-sodium beef broth
ingredients.note: Use plain unsalted beef broth at about 60 mg sodium per cup, with household-approved ingredients.

ingredients.name: table salt
ingredients.note: Fine table salt, about 590 mg sodium per 1/4 teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1/16 tsp total.

steps.title: Brown the roux
steps.text: Melt {bf} in the skillet over medium-low heat. Whisk in {fl} for 3–4 minutes until the roux turns the color of toasted bread.

steps.title: Whisk in the broth
steps.text: Slowly whisk in {be}, then add {al}, {nut}, {wp} and {salt}. Simmer for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Finish the cream gravy
steps.text: Whisk in {milk} and {cc}. Warm gently for 2–3 minutes, until smooth enough to coat a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Ladle over meatballs, mashed potatoes or soft noodles cooked in the gravy with enough added water to soften them.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1/16 tsp table salt in place of 1/4 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. The milk sauce can separate or become grainy when frozen. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, omit the white pepper and halve the allspice. For dairy-free gravy, use avocado oil, unsweetened oat milk and plain whipped dairy-free cream cheese. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 52 kcal, 1.7 g protein, 2.9 g total carbohydrate, 3.7 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 175 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 52 kcal, 1.7 g protein, 2.9 g total carbohydrate, 3.7 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 65 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.
